scoring_rules.json.scientific_requirements: Score independently established final scientific propositions only, totaling 100 points (paper_science_v3 / final_results_100). Each item receives all its points on pass and zero on fail or need_review. No independent process, workflow, structure-delivery, calculation-count or chronology points. Native evidence qualifies the affected proposition, not an additional score. Match identity, electronic state, physical quantity, units, reference and environment. Supplied facts and copied source targets are not newly computed findings. Hard numeric windows are unchanged and binary; missing calculation, wrong identity/reference/unit, unsupported guesses and out-of-window numbers fail. A scientifically established equivalent explanation passes directly. Only the concrete unresolved scientific conflicts named in an item can receive need_review; review is not success. All listed outcomes are required for whole-case success. Judge evidence claim by claim, without a mandatory author intermediate sequence or universal validation matrix.

items.statement: Terminal nitrogen addition creates the entrance complex
items.expected: Actual finite approach/connection evidence supports the SiN nitrogen center adding to a terminal carbon of intact isoprene and reaching the open-chain addition intermediate on a neutral doublet surface. An optimized adduct alone does not establish this addition connection; a finite supported entry is sufficient without a global infinite-separation barrierlessness proof.

items.statement: Ring closure connects the addition adduct to a six-membered intermediate
items.expected: A physically validated connection from an appropriately oriented open-chain N-addition adduct closes a C–Si bond into the six-membered ring corresponding to the i1-cis→i2 transformation. Endpoint identity and reaction motion/connection must agree; labels, a reaction sketch or energy proximity alone are insufficient.

items.statement: Hydrogen migration to nitrogen preserves the viable cyclic route
items.expected: Computed connection evidence supports migration of the relevant cyclic intermediate hydrogen to nitrogen, corresponding to i2→i4, on the same doublet surface. Its transition structure is below separated reactants in consistent E0 even though the local barrier is positive. A source-prose number alone does not establish the step.

items.statement: Hydrogen migration to silicon reaches the H-loss precursor
items.expected: Computed connection evidence supports the subsequent carbon-to-silicon hydrogen migration corresponding to i4→i5 while retaining the methyl spectator and cyclic skeleton. This is a separate chemical connection from migration to nitrogen.

items.statement: Silicon hydrogen loss reaches the P1 product basin
items.expected: Actual dissociation/connection evidence supports loss of the silicon-bound H from the connected cyclic precursor to the P1 skeleton plus H. The retained heavy-atom framework must approach the validated product; a finite sampled release may establish the bounded result without claiming a globally barrierless asymptote.

items.condition: Demonstrated fabricated computational evidence or unauthorized access to hidden evaluator answers invalidates the submission. Mere failure, missing files, an incorrect state, numerical disagreement, or an unsupported claim does not by itself establish fabrication.
Wrong composition, charge/spin, energy definition, connectivity, unsupported or contradictory evidence fails only the affected scientific leaf; no global zero for an ordinary local failure.

reference_qualification.json.acceptance_basis: Historical computations reused proposition by proposition as documented in the 2026-10-28 prefix and modification report. Previous PASS or qualified acceptance is not a new V3 whole-case validation.
reference_qualification.json.scientific_scope: Same isolated-gas SiN/isoprene H-loss question: two source-supported products and their E0, a bounded connected formation explanation and product identifiability; no new network or control matrix.
publication_or_expert_review_limits: The source itself gives i2→i4 barrier140 in prose versus142 from Fig5, while actual is148.7503075743 kJ/mol; the gap remains a disclosed mismatch with no fitted window or invented causal explanation.

Finite source-oriented entry and exit connections are supported. Infinite-separation barrierlessness, all38 isomers, a complete P2 network, absolute rates and branching fractions are outside the accepted result.

The experimental energy interval tests channel compatibility, not thermodynamic 298 K equilibrium or local barrier accuracy. Composite spin contamination and unavailable source TS definition remain visible.
reference_qualification.json.historical_status_policy: Prior pending/strict numerical failure records are preserved history, not current runtime gating.
reference_qualification.json.evidence_reuse_note: r_p1_structure/p2_structure and r_p1_exoergicity/p2_exoergicity reuse P1/P2_CBS_verification and P1_P2_H_asymptote_comparison_20260930.json: E0=-156.4325195194/-150.5408983284 kJ/mol within unchanged [-189,-135]. r_formation_account reuses P1_ROUTE_EDGE_AUDIT.json and connected-edge native CBS/IRC/LQA/exit evidence, without making its author node sequence mandatory. r_product_identifiability follows from the overlap and bounded route coverage. The i2→i4 local barrier is 148.7503076 kJ/mol versus source prose140/Fig5-derived142; it is still -40.6059774 relative to reactants. This mismatch, finite exit/entry sampling and composite spin contamination remain unresolved limits. The full P2 network, all38 isomers and rates are not claimed.
reference_qualification.json.second_audit_candidate_coverage: Second audit: the public comparison now explicitly addresses two inequivalent diene/SiN orientations, without supplying product graphs, ring size, entry atom or a winning mechanism. Existing evidence covers two specific P1/P2 endpoints and a finite P1 route, not the whole product space. Source-specific required endpoints versus independent AR alternatives remain an expert issue. Do not silently apply P1/P2 windows to another product or claim whole-space exclusion.
